title: A kayaking course booking
description: Original IELTS-inspired mini-drill with a single synthetic voice; not an official test or band predictor. Read the 8 questions, listen once, submit your answers, then replay and check the transcript. Notice corrections and distinguish included services from extras.
passage:
Hello, this is Lena from Riverway Outdoor Centre, returning your call about the kayaking course. You mentioned that you have never tried the sport, so I have reserved a place on the beginner course. Our intermediate group would require previous experience.

Your session is on Thursday. I originally said Tuesday, but the instructor is attending a training event that day. Please arrive at 9:45 to collect your equipment. The activity itself begins at ten, and we cannot admit anyone after the safety briefing.

We used to meet at the boathouse. Because work is being done on its roof, your group should meet at the visitor centre. The sign at the main gate shows the way. Your instructor's surname is Morgan; that is M, O, R, G, A, N.

The adult course costs 38 pounds. There is a reduced student price of 32 pounds, but you said you are booking as an adult. Transport from the centre to the river is included. Lunch is not, and waterproof jackets are available for an additional charge. Bring your own drinking water.

Finally, ordinary rain will not stop us. If the river becomes unsafe, we will run an indoor safety workshop instead. We will not simply move the booking to another week. Please call if your contact number changes.

questions.question: Which course has been reserved?
questions.explanation: Lena says she has reserved a place on the beginner course because the listener has never tried kayaking. The intermediate group requires experience.

questions.question: The session is on _____. Write ONE WORD.
questions.explanation: Thursday is the confirmed day. Tuesday is the original information and is explicitly corrected.

questions.question: Arrival time for collecting equipment: _____. Write A NUMBER.
questions.explanation: Arrive at 9:45 to collect equipment. Ten is the activity start time, not the arrival time.

questions.question: Where should this group meet?
questions.explanation: The boathouse is the old meeting place. Roof work means the group should now meet at the visitor centre; the main gate only has a sign.

questions.question: Instructor's surname: _____. Write ONE WORD.
questions.explanation: The surname is given and then spelled M, O, R, G, A, N.

questions.question: Adult course price: £_____. Write A NUMBER.
questions.explanation: The adult course costs 38 pounds. The 32-pound price is for students.

questions.question: Which service is included in the course price?
options: Transport from the centre to the river
questions.answer: Transport from the centre to the river
questions.explanation: Transport is included. Lunch is not included, and waterproof jackets cost extra.

questions.question: What will happen if the river becomes unsafe?
options: a replacement session the following week
questions.explanation: Unsafe river conditions lead to an indoor safety workshop. Ordinary rain alone does not stop the activity, and moving to another week is explicitly rejected.

title: New students on campus
description: Original IELTS-inspired campus announcement with a single synthetic voice; not an official test or band predictor. Read the 8 questions first. Listen for room numbers, quantities and the final arrangement when the speaker changes a detail.
passage:
Welcome to Westbridge College. Before we begin the campus tour, I need to explain a few arrangements for your first week. Tomorrow's induction starts at ten. Your welcome email says room 207, but the group is larger than expected, so please use room 214 instead. Both rooms are on the second floor.

You may have noticed that the main library is closed. This is because of electrical repairs, rather than a shortage of staff. A temporary borrowing desk is operating in the student centre. New students can borrow up to 6 books at a time. That limit increases later in the year.

Your student card also gives you 10 pounds of printing credit. Extra credit can be purchased online. For anyone cycling to college, the new bicycle racks are behind the sports hall. The spaces beside the station belong to the railway company.

The careers team welcomes visitors without appointments this week, but you must arrive before 11 in the morning. After that, advisers will be interviewing applicants.

The shared kitchen is open all day. It is busiest between twelve and one, so eating slightly later may be more comfortable. Finally, if you cannot connect your laptop to the college network, book an online appointment with the computer support team. Taking it directly to reception will not get you technical help.

questions.question: Room for tomorrow's induction: _____. Write A NUMBER.
questions.explanation: Room 207 appears in the old email, but the larger group will use room 214 instead.

questions.question: Why is the main library closed?
questions.explanation: The speaker explicitly gives electrical repairs as the cause and rejects staff shortage. The larger group explains the induction room change.

questions.question: Maximum books a new student can borrow now: _____. Write A NUMBER.
questions.explanation: New students can borrow up to 6 books at a time. A later increase does not change the current limit.

questions.question: Printing credit on the student card: £_____. Write A NUMBER.
questions.explanation: The student card provides 10 pounds of printing credit; additional credit has to be purchased.

questions.question: Where are the college's new bicycle racks?
questions.explanation: The college's new racks are behind the sports hall. The spaces beside the station are owned by the railway company, while the student centre has the borrowing desk.

questions.question: To visit careers advisers without an appointment this week, arrive before _____ a.m. Write A NUMBER.
questions.explanation: Visitors without appointments must arrive before 11 in the morning. After that, the advisers have interviews.

questions.question: When is the shared kitchen busiest?
questions.explanation: The kitchen is open all day, but its busiest period is between twelve and one. Opening hours and peak use are different details.

questions.question: What should students do if a laptop cannot connect to the college network?
options: take the laptop straight to reception
questions.explanation: Students should book an online appointment with computer support. Reception will not provide technical help, and the induction is not offered as a solution to this problem.

title: Planning a local history project
description: Original IELTS-inspired project briefing with a single synthetic voice; not an official test or band predictor. Read the questions, listen once and distinguish the team's final decisions from rejected ideas. Review the evidence after submitting.
passage:
Here is the final plan for our local history project. We considered analysing newspaper articles, but our tutor suggested interviews with residents because personal memories would give us a different kind of evidence. We will still read a little background material before meeting anyone.

At first, we hoped to recruit thirty people. That would take too long, so our target is now 24 participants. We want a mixture of ages, although everyone must have lived in the town for at least five years.

The tutor checked our draft questions yesterday. She thought the topics were relevant, but several questions were too technical. We need to replace specialist terms with everyday language. She did not ask us to add more questions.

Each interview should last about 15 minutes. The original idea was half an hour, but volunteers may struggle to spare that much time. We have permission to use a quiet room at the museum. A café would be convenient, but background noise would make the recordings difficult to understand.

Please finish revising the questions by Friday. Our pilot interview is on Saturday, which gives us one day to prepare. Its main purpose is to test the recording equipment, since we have not used these microphones before. After collecting all the interviews, each pair will write a summary. Keep that summary to a maximum of 600 words, excluding the list of sources.

questions.question: What will be the project's main source of evidence?
questions.explanation: The tutor recommended interviews with residents for personal memories. Newspaper analysis was considered, and background reading remains only preparation.

questions.question: Current recruitment target: _____ participants. Write A NUMBER.
questions.explanation: Thirty was the original hope. The current target is 24 because recruiting thirty would take too long.

questions.question: What problem did the tutor identify in the draft questions?
questions.explanation: Several questions were too technical, so specialist terms need simpler wording. The tutor does not describe the questions as personal or repetitive.

questions.question: Planned length of each interview: _____ minutes. Write A NUMBER.
questions.explanation: The final plan is about 15 minutes. Half an hour was the original idea and was rejected because of volunteers' time.

questions.question: Where will the interviews take place?
questions.explanation: The team has permission to use a quiet room at the museum. The café is rejected because background noise would harm the recordings. No library location is proposed.

questions.question: Deadline for revising the questions: _____. Write ONE WORD.
questions.explanation: The revisions are due by Friday. Saturday is the pilot interview date, a separate event.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the pilot interview?
questions.explanation: The speaker explicitly identifies testing the unfamiliar recording equipment as the pilot's main purpose.

questions.question: Maximum summary length, excluding sources: _____ words. Write A NUMBER.
questions.explanation: Each pair's summary has a maximum of 600 words. The sources list is excluded from that limit.
